interest: FBI tracking of pro-Axis Japanese in Peru and Paraguay.
overview: This file (State Department decimal 894.20234) contains intelligence reports, transmittal correspondence, and diplomatic telegrams from late 1944 through late 1945 regarding Japanese civilian, educational, and diplomatic activities in South America, focusing primarily on Peru, Paraguay, and Argentina. The bulk of the material consists of Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) reports transmitted by Director J. Edgar Hoover to Frederick B. Lyon of the State Department's Division of Foreign Activity Correlation. In Peru, reports detail the activities of Julio Hoshi (Teruo Hoshi), a prominent Peruvian-born Nisei who directed the Escuela Zamudio (formerly Hoshi-Gaku-En), engaged in commercial cloaking via dummy agents to evade the U.S. Proclaimed List, and allegedly served as an informant for the Spanish Embassy while intimidating pro-Allied Japanese and Okinawans. In Paraguay, an intelligence report documents government surveillance and the formal expropriation of Japanese school real estate and assets at Colonia La Colmena near Ybytymí following presidential decrees in August 1945. The file concludes with communications concerning Argentina, including a Department of State telegram directing the U.S. Embassy in Buenos Aires to investigate Japanese diplomats' post-rupture activities and non-enforcement of wartime restrictions.

subfiles.about: Transmittal letter from FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover forwarding an intelligence report on Julio Hoshi to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Hoover sends a report on Julio Hoshi, a pro-Japanese Nisei in Lima said to inform the Spanish Embassy on disloyal Japanese.
subfiles.title: FBI Transmittal Letter regarding Julio Hoshi in Lima, Peru

subfiles.about: Investigative report detailing the pro-Japanese background, clandestine schooling, Proclaimed List evasion, and community influence of Julio Hoshi in Lima, Peru.
keywords: Sociedad Ex-Alumnos de la Escuela Japonesa
subfiles.summary: FBI report on Julio Hoshi of Lima, who ran a school teaching Japanese patriotism, used a front man to evade the Proclaimed List and threatened Okinawans.
subfiles.title: FBI Investigative Report on Julio Hoshi (alias Teruo Hoshi), Lima, Peru

subfiles.about: Transmittal letter from the FBI forwarding an intelligence report concerning the Japanese agricultural settlement at Ybytymí, Paraguay.
subfiles.summary: FBI sends State a memo on the Japanese colony at Ybytymí, Paraguay.
subfiles.title: FBI Transmittal Letter regarding Japanese Colony at Ybytymí, Paraguay

subfiles.about: Investigative report on the government oversight, dissolution, and asset expropriation of the Japanese school at Colonia La Colmena near Ybytymí, Paraguay.
subfiles.summary: FBI report: Paraguay's 1945 decrees expropriated the Japanese school at Colonia La Colmena and handed it to the Ministry of Education.
subfiles.title: FBI Report on Japanese Colony at Ybytymí, Paraguay

subfiles.about: Concluding page of a memorandum discussing an Argentine publication and political identification.
subfiles.summary: Second page of an incomplete memo citing an Argentine publication, with a routing note to Mr. Hussey.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Fragment regarding Argentine Publication

subfiles.about: State Department telegram instructing the U.S. Embassy in Buenos Aires to report on non-enforcement of diplomatic restrictions and abuses of liberty by Japanese diplomats in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: State asks Buenos Aires for evidence of Japanese diplomats' activities and Argentine laxity since the break in relations, for an upcoming conference, plus missing press summaries.
subfiles.title: State Department Telegram No. 139 to Embassy Buenos Aires regarding Japanese Diplomats
